site.anchor: cabe a suspensão do art. 77, § 2º
provisions: CP art. 77, caput, I a III

source.quote: § 2o A execução da pena privativa de liberdade, não superior a quatro anos, poderá ser suspensa, por quatro a seis anos, desde que o condenado seja maior de setenta anos de idade, ou razões de saúde justifiquem a suspensão.

citations.cite: CP art. 77, caput, I a III

readings.description: § 2º moves the caput's limits (a penalty of up to four years, a period of four to six) and adds its own condition (over seventy, or health); the caput's incisos I–III still apply to it.

citations.cite: CP art. 77, caput — the incisos are the requirements of 'A execução ... poderá ser suspensa'
CP art. 77, § 1º — a paragraph of the same article, read with inciso I

readings.description: § 2º is self-contained: its own 'desde que' lists the only conditions, so a repeat offender in an intentional crime over seventy, or one for whom art. 44's substitution is available, qualifies.

citations.cite: CP art. 77, § 2º — 'desde que o condenado seja maior de setenta anos de idade, ou razões de saúde justifiquem a suspensão'

readings.rejection_rationale: It would deny the suspension to a repeat offender sentenced to two years under the caput and grant it to the same offender sentenced to four under § 2º, and would let § 2º bypass inciso III's rule that the suspension yields to art. 44's substitution. A paragraph is read with its caput unless it says otherwise.

taken.rationale: § 2º is a paragraph of art. 77 and changes only what it names: the maximum penalty, the period, and an added condition. Nothing in it dispenses with the requirements the caput sets for every suspension.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `três anos, doente e reincidente` — § 2º not available

site.anchor: as modalidades de suspensão cabíveis (art. 77)

source.quote: A execução da pena privativa de liberdade, não superior a 2 (dois) anos, poderá ser suspensa, por 2 (dois) a 4 (quatro) anos, desde que:

citations.cite: CP art. 77, § 2º — 'não superior a quatro anos'

readings.description: A penalty of two years or less imposed on a convict over seventy (or with health reasons) meets both the caput and § 2º; both are returned and the judge chooses.

citations.cite: CP art. 77, § 2º — 'não superior a quatro anos' includes two years or less

readings.description: § 2º exists to extend the suspension to penalties over two and up to four years; for two years or less only the caput (two to four years of probation) applies, since § 2º's longer period would make the benefit harsher for the very group it favours.
readings.foreclosure: § 2º's words, 'não superior a quatro anos', reach a penalty of two years or less, and the Code does not rank the two paragraphs. A court could still read § 2º teleologically.

taken.rationale: Both paragraphs' words reach the case and the Code does not rank them. Returning both leaves to the judge a choice the Code gives the judge ('poderá'); picking the caput would decide a question the text does not.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `um ano, Vicente aos setenta` — both modalities listed

site.anchor: cabe a suspensão do art. 77, § 2º

source.quote: desde que o condenado seja maior de setenta anos de idade

citations.cite: CP art. 115 — 'na data da sentença', where the Code names the date

readings.description: The age is taken on the date of the decision that grants the suspension — the sentence.

citations.cite: CP art. 77, § 2º — 'o condenado seja': a status of the convict when the suspension is decided

readings.description: The age is taken on the date of the offence, as for the atenuante of art. 65, I's first limb.
readings.rejection_rationale: Art. 77, § 2º speaks of 'o condenado', a status that exists only once there is a conviction; where the Code wants the date of the offence it says 'ao tempo do crime' (art. 115) or 'na data do fato' (art. 65, I).

taken.rationale: The paragraph describes the convict at the moment the suspension is decided, and names no other date.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `três anos, Vicente no aniversário de setenta` and `três anos, Vicente na véspera`

site.anchor: há causa de revogação obrigatória (art. 81, caput)

source.quote: I - é condenado, em sentença irrecorrível, por crime doloso;

readings.description: A final conviction for an intentional crime revokes the suspension whatever the penalty, a fine included.

citations.cite: CP art. 81, caput, I — no penalty named
CP art. 81, § 1º — which does name the penalties, for negligent crimes and misdemeanours

readings.description: A conviction to a fine only does not revoke, by analogy with art. 77, § 1º, under which an earlier conviction to a fine does not bar the grant.
readings.foreclosure: Art. 81 names penalties in § 1º and none in inciso I, so the text distinguishes the two; the analogy with art. 77, § 1º concerns the grant, not revocation.

taken.rationale: Inciso I is unqualified, and the next paragraph shows the drafter qualifying by penalty where it meant to.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `a suspensão, doloso só multa` — obligatory

site.anchor: a condenação é irrecorrível no curso do prazo

source.quote: A suspensão será revogada se, no curso do prazo, o beneficiário:

readings.description: What must fall within the period is the conviction becoming final ('é condenado, em sentença irrecorrível'), whenever the crime was committed; the period includes any extension under § 2º.

citations.cite: CP art. 81, § 2º — the period is extended until the final judgment of a prosecution under way, which only matters if the conviction, not the crime, has to fall within it

readings.description: What must fall within the period is the offence; a conviction for an offence committed during it revokes whenever it becomes final.
readings.rejection_rationale: Inciso I describes the beneficiary being convicted, not offending, and § 2º's extension would be pointless if a later conviction for an offence in the period revoked anyway.

taken.rationale: The verb is 'é condenado, em sentença irrecorrível', and § 2º extends the period precisely so that a conviction still pending at its end can fall within it.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `a suspensão, doloso no último dia` and `a suspensão, doloso no dia seguinte`
cp-g1c-livramento-condicional-testes.l4: `o livramento, condenação depois do fim` — no ground
notes: The same reading is taken for the livramento (arts. 86–87, `a condenação é irrecorrível na vigência do livramento`): the conviction must become final while the livramento runs; art. 86 says separately when the crime must have been committed.

site.anchor: há causa de revogação obrigatória (art. 81, caput)

source.quote: II - frustra, embora solvente, a execução de pena de multa ou não efetua, sem motivo justificado, a reparação do dano;

readings.description: Frustrating, while solvent, the enforcement of a fine revokes the suspension, as printed.

citations.cite: CP art. 81, caput, II — unamended since 1984

readings.description: Since Lei nº 9.268/1996 made the fine a debt collected under the rules for public debts (art. 51), frustrating its enforcement can no longer be a ground of revocation, and this part of inciso II is tacitly revoked.
readings.foreclosure: The compiled text keeps the words with no revocation note, and ADI 7.032 (M-sweep-a-03) has since read art. 51 as keeping the fine's penal character — an unpaid cumulative fine bars extinção da punibilidade. A court could still hold the ground spent.

taken.rationale: The words are in force as printed; the tacit-revocation argument needs an authority this encoding's sources do not carry, and the only one the sweep found (ADI 7.032) points the other way.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `a suspensão, multa frustrada` — obligatory

site.anchor: o último dia do período de prova, prorrogado (art. 81, § 2º)

source.quote: § 2º - Se o beneficiário está sendo processado por outro crime ou contravenção, considera-se prorrogado o prazo da suspensão até o julgamento definitivo.

readings.description: One 'está sendo processado' from the receipt of the denúncia or queixa until the final judgment.

citations.cite: CP art. 81, § 2º — 'processado', a prosecution, not an investigation

readings.description: One is 'being processed' from the opening of a police investigation.
readings.rejection_rationale: An inquérito is not a processo; the paragraph speaks of a prosecution ending in a 'julgamento definitivo'.

readings.description: One is 'being processed' from the offering of the denúncia, before a court receives it.
readings.foreclosure: Until the court receives the charge there is no prosecution before it; the difference is the days between offering and receipt.

taken.rationale: The receipt of the charge is the act that makes a processo exist before a court, and it is the date the criminal record shows.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `a suspensão com processo posterior` (received after the end: no extension)

site.anchor: a pena privativa de liberdade está extinta pelo art. 82

source.quote: Art. 82 - Expirado o prazo sem que tenha havido revogação, considera-se extinta a pena privativa de liberdade.

readings.description: An obligatory cause of revocation that arose during the period bars the extinction even if the judge had not decreed the revocation before the period ended; the judge must still revoke.

citations.cite: CP art. 81, caput — 'A suspensão será revogada se, no curso do prazo, ...'

readings.description: Only a revocation decreed before the period expires bars the extinction; once the period has run with no revocation decreed, the penalty is extinct, whatever happened during it.

citations.cite: CP art. 82 — 'sem que tenha havido revogação'

readings.foreclosure: Art. 81's caput makes revocation mandatory and ties it to what happened 'no curso do prazo', not to the date of the decree; reading art. 82 alone would let the court's delay defeat a mandatory rule. Case law on revocation after the period was not retrieved for this encoding.

taken.rationale: Art. 81 says the suspension 'será revogada' for causes arising in the period; art. 82's 'sem que tenha havido revogação' is read with that command, not against it. A facultative cause the judge did not use does not bar the extinction.

witnesses: cp-g1c-suspensao-condicional-testes.l4: `a suspensão com crime doloso` in 2029 — not extinct; `a suspensão, outra condição descumprida` — extinct
notes: Arts. 82 and 90 extinguish the CUSTODIAL penalty. Whether punibilidade is extinct while a cumulative fine is unpaid is art. 51's question, read under ADI 7.032 (M-sweep-a-03) by art. 51's encoder (g1b); art. 80 says the suspension never reached the fine.

site.anchor: a fração exigida para a pena (art. 83)

source.quote: I - cumprida mais de um terço da pena se o condenado não for reincidente em crime doloso e tiver bons antecedentes;

readings.description: A convict who is not a repeat offender in an intentional crime and has no good record falls in neither inciso: I requires a good record, II requires repeat offending. The Code names no fraction for the case; the encoding refuses rather than pick one.
More than one third, as for the primary convict: II reaches only repeat offenders, and a gap in a rule restricting liberty is closed in the convict's favour.
readings.foreclosure: Inciso I's words require 'bons antecedentes', which this convict lacks. Case law closing the gap either way was not retrieved for this encoding.

readings.description: More than one half, by analogy with II: a convict with a bad record is treated like the repeat offender.
readings.foreclosure: Inciso II's words require repeat offending in an intentional crime, which this convict lacks, and an analogy against the convict in a rule restricting liberty is doubtful.

taken.rationale: Neither inciso reaches the case, and choosing between one third and one half would be the encoder deciding a question the Code leaves open. The refusal is returned by name, so a caller sees exactly which case it is.

witnesses: cp-g1c-livramento-condicional-testes.l4: `primário sem bons antecedentes` — REFUSED

site.anchor: o tempo de pena a ser superado (arts. 83 e 84)
provisions: CP art. 83, I, II e V

source.quote: Art. 84 - As penas que correspondem a infrações diversas devem somar-se para efeito do livramento.

citations.cite: CP art. 83, V — 'nos casos de condenação por crime hediondo ...'

readings.description: Each penalty carries the fraction its crime calls for (two thirds for V's crimes, one third or one half for the others) and the parts are added; the total must be exceeded.

citations.cite: CP art. 83, V — the fraction attaches to 'condenação por' the listed crimes

readings.description: The penalties are added first and one fraction applies to the sum — the heaviest any of them calls for.
readings.rejection_rationale: It would make a common crime's penalty wait two thirds because the convict also serves a V penalty, which V does not say; art. 84 adds the penalties 'para efeito do livramento' without choosing a fraction for the sum.

taken.rationale: V ties its fraction to the conviction for the listed crimes, not to the convict; art. 84 adds the penalties. Adding the parts is the reading that honours both.

witnesses: cp-g1c-livramento-condicional-testes.l4: `uma do inciso V e uma comum` — three years required

site.anchor: sem falta grave nos últimos 12 meses (art. 83, III, b)

source.quote: b) não cometimento de falta grave nos últimos 12 (doze) meses; (Incluído pela Lei nº 13.964, de 2019)

readings.description: A falta is 'nos últimos 12 meses' while the twelve-month term that begins on the day of the falta (art. 10, the first day counting) has not run by the day of the decision.

citations.cite: CP art. 10 — 'O dia do começo inclui-se no cômputo do prazo'

readings.description: The window is the twelve months ending on the day of the decision, counted back from it.
readings.rejection_rationale: It gives the same days as the first reading when counted by the calendar, but counting back from a date invites month subtraction, which clamps (PLAN trap T9); the first reading is the same window counted forward.

taken.rationale: Art. 10 counts every term of the Code; counted forward from the falta, the twelve months end on the day before the anniversary, so a falta a full year before the decision no longer bars.

notes: Boundary tests: cp-g1c-livramento-condicional-testes.l4, `falta em junho de 2025, decisão em 31 de maio` (bars) and `... decisão em 1º de junho` (does not).

site.anchor: há o motivo do art. 86, II

source.quote: II - por crime anterior, observado o disposto no art. 84 deste Código.

readings.description: A final custodial conviction for a crime before the livramento revokes it only if, the new penalty added to the others (art. 84), the time served — counting the time on livramento, which art. 88 discounts in this case — no longer exceeds the fraction required.

citations.cite: CP art. 86, II — 'observado o disposto no art. 84'
CP art. 88 — the time free is discounted when the revocation results from a conviction for an earlier crime

readings.description: Any such conviction revokes; the reference to art. 84 only says the penalties are then served as one.
readings.rejection_rationale: It leaves 'observado o disposto no art. 84' with nothing to do at the moment of revocation, and treats an earlier crime exactly like a crime committed on livramento, which the article separates into two incisos.

taken.rationale: The reference to art. 84 in the inciso that concerns earlier crimes has work to do only if the summed penalty is tested against the time served; art. 88 says what that time includes.

witnesses: cp-g1c-livramento-condicional-testes.l4: `o livramento, crime anterior leve` (not revoked) and `o livramento, crime anterior grave` (revoked)
notes: The time on livramento is counted as the days from release to the day the conviction became final, converted at thirty days to a month — the Duração convention (PLAN § 2.1) — not by the calendar.

site.anchor: há condenação a pena não privativa de liberdade (art. 87)

source.quote: Art. 87 - O juiz poderá, também, revogar o livramento, se o liberado deixar de cumprir qualquer das obrigações constantes da sentença, ou for irrecorrivelmente condenado, por crime ou contravenção, a pena que não seja privativa de liberdade.

citations.cite: CP art. 86, caput — 'condenado a pena privativa de liberdade ... por crime'

readings.description: A final conviction for a misdemeanour to a custodial penalty (prisão simples) is a ground in neither article: art. 86 speaks of a crime, art. 87 of a penalty that is not custodial.
A fortiori: if a non-custodial conviction for a misdemeanour lets the judge revoke, a custodial one must too.
readings.foreclosure: The article names 'pena que não seja privativa de liberdade', and a ground for revoking a benefit is not extended by analogy against the convict. The a fortiori argument is available to a court.

taken.rationale: The two articles are drafted to be read together and leave this case out; the encoding does not add a ground of revocation the text does not state.

witnesses: cp-g1c-livramento-condicional-testes.l4: `o livramento, contravenção com prisão` — no ground

site.anchor: o livramento revogado pode ser novamente concedido (art. 88)

source.quote: Art. 88 - Revogado o livramento, não poderá ser novamente concedido, e, salvo quando a revogação resulta de condenação por outro crime anterior àquele benefício, não se desconta na pena o tempo em que esteve solto o condenado.

readings.description: After any revocation, the livramento cannot be granted again, as printed.
Where the revocation results from a conviction for an earlier crime, a new livramento may be granted on the summed penalties.

citations.cite: CP art. 88, segunda parte — which already treats that case apart

readings.foreclosure: The Code's first limb is unqualified. The Lei de Execução Penal (art. 141), outside this encoding's sources, is read in practice as permitting a new livramento in that case; a court applying it would take this reading.

taken.rationale: The encoding carries the Code's words; the Lei de Execução Penal is not among its sources, and the qualification the second limb makes does not reach the first.

site.anchor: cumpriu mais do que o tempo exigido (art. 83)

source.quote: b) não cometimento de falta grave nos últimos 12 (doze) meses; (Incluído pela Lei nº 13.964, de 2019)

readings.description: No: the fraction runs from the start of execution regardless; since 2019 a falta grave in the last twelve months is a separate bar under art. 83, III, b.
Yes: the fraction is counted afresh from the last falta grave.
readings.rejection_rationale: Struck by Súmula 441 STJ (M-sweep-a-28); since 2019 the falta also has its own inciso, III, b, so restarting the fraction would count it twice.

source.quote: Art. 89 - O juiz não poderá declarar extinta a pena, enquanto não passar em julgado a sentença em processo a que responde o liberado, por crime cometido na vigência do livramento.

readings.description: Yes: absent suspension or revocation before the período de prova ends, punibilidade is extinct (art. 90); art. 89 operates only through a timely suspension.
No: art. 89 bars extinction whenever such a prosecution is pending, whether or not the livramento was suspended.
readings.rejection_rationale: Struck by Súmula 617 STJ (M-sweep-a-29): art. 89 works only through a suspension decreed before the período de prova ends.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 617 STJ. A revocation decreed after the end, with no suspension before it, is also too late on the same reasoning; a revocation after a timely suspension still counts.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 617 STJ: 'A ausência de suspensão ou revogação do livramento condicional antes do término do período de prova enseja a extinção da punibilidade pelo integral cumprimento da pena.' (julgado em 26/09/2018, DJe 01/10/2018)

site.anchor: a lei comina pena máxima superior a 6 anos de reclusão (art. 91-A)

source.quote: Na hipótese de condenação por infrações às quais a lei comine pena máxima superior a 6 (seis) anos de reclusão

citations.cite: CP art. 91-A, caput (incluído pela Lei nº 13.964/2019)
CP art. 109, caput — 'o máximo da pena privativa de liberdade cominada ao crime'

readings.description: The maximum is the pena cominada's with the case's causes of increase and decrease applied at their outer limits — the 'pena em abstrato' that art. 109 reads.

citations.cite: PLAN § 2.3 — `a pena cominada com as causas`

source.quote: I – aplicados os efeitos previstos nos incisos I e II do caput deste artigo;

CP art. 92, I, a e b

site.anchor: Parte Geral, arts. 77 a 120 — o que os capítulos de g1c compartilham

source.quote: Parágrafo único - A lei posterior, que de qualquer modo favorecer o agente, aplica-se aos fatos anteriores, ainda que decididos por sentença condenatória transitada em julgado.

readings.description: Where a later law made one of these provisions harsher, the date that decides which wording governs is the date of the crime: for an earlier crime the earlier wording governs — a paragraph added later does not apply, and a provision re-worded later refuses, since the text it replaced is not in the source.

citations.cite: CP art. 2º, parágrafo único — the more favourable later law reaches earlier facts; the harsher one does not
CP art. 4º — the time of the crime is the moment of the action or omission

readings.description: The provisions on execution, effects, decadência and prescription are procedural or executory, and the wording in force at the decision governs.
readings.foreclosure: Prescription, decadência, the effects of conviction and the conditions of the benefits all bear on how much of the penalty is suffered, and are treated as penal law, which does not reach back when harsher. A court classing one of them as procedural would apply the later wording.

taken.rationale: Every provision gated in this encoding bears on punishment: whether and how long it is served, and what follows from it. Art. 2º says a more favourable later law reaches back; a harsher one therefore does not.

A later law that made a provision MORE favourable reaches earlier facts under art. 2º, parágrafo único; no rule here is gated on such a change.

The conductor's rulings of 2026-09-30 (PLAN § 10, strict): a provision re-worded later refuses for EVERY earlier fact, even one its present words would not reach, because what the earlier wording said is in no bundled source. Applied to art. 115 (every crime before 4.7.2025), art. 92, II (every fact before 10.10.2024) and art. 92, § 2º (every fact from 10.10.2024 to 6.8.2026, a refusal that reaches art. 92, I and the list of effects in that window). The refused assertions were kept, flipped to #ASSERT REFUSED with the reason, each still carrying the answer the present words give.

Measured cost, art. 115 — strict gate: 36 of 119 prescription assertions refuse; no prescription is computable for a crime before 4.7.2025 until the vintage pass brings the pre-2025 art. 115 into the bundle. The count was taken on the suite as it stood at the ruling. Fifteen post-amendment twin assertions (crimes of 2025–2030) were then added, so that the count, art. 110, § 1º, the third for the repeat offender and art. 117, V's stop are still exercised: 12 of 12 prescription mutations caught. Every prescription passes through art. 115, which is why the cost is so wide, and that is the argument for bringing arts. 115 and 92 into the bundle first in the vintage pass.

Measured cost, art. 92, § 2º: in the tests as they stood, one assertion changed (a fact of 1.1.2025 that the present words do not reach); two more were added for the spread to art. 92, I and the list of effects. Art. 92, I still answers TRUE in that window where its own thresholds are met, because its 'ou' is decided before § 2º is consulted.

site.anchor: o fato é punível com detenção (art. 97)

source.quote: Se, todavia, o fato previsto como crime for punível com detenção, poderá o juiz submetê-lo a tratamento ambulatorial.

citations.cite: CP art. 235, § 1º; art. 306, parágrafo único — the preceitos that leave the species to the judge

readings.description: 'Punível com detenção' where the preceito prescribes detenção or leaves the species to the judge between reclusão and detenção; not where it prescribes reclusão alone, nor where it prescribes a fine only.
An act punishable only with a fine is a fortiori open to outpatient treatment: if the lighter custodial species allows it, a penalty with no custody at all must.
readings.foreclosure: The words name detenção; the only fine-only preceito in the Code (art. 146-A) is recent, and whether a medida de segurança fits it at all is a question the text does not raise. A court could adopt the a fortiori reading.

readings.description: Outpatient treatment is open whatever the species, the choice following the medical need rather than the penalty.
readings.foreclosure: The caput ties the exception to detenção in terms. STJ case law said to allow outpatient treatment for acts punishable with reclusão was not retrieved by the sweep and is not a source of this encoding; it is recorded as an open question in notes/g1c.md.

taken.rationale: The caput says 'punível com detenção'. A preceito that lets the judge impose detenção makes the act punishable with it; one of reclusão alone, or of a fine alone, does not.

witnesses: cp-g1c-medidas-de-seguranca-testes.l4: `espécie ao juiz, até 3` (both measures) and `só multa` (committal only)

site.anchor: as medidas que podem substituir a pena (art. 98)

source.quote: a pena privativa de liberdade pode ser substituída pela internação, ou tratamento ambulatorial, pelo prazo mínimo de 1 (um) a 3 (três) anos, nos termos do artigo anterior e respectivos §§ 1º a 4º.

readings.description: For the partly responsible convict both measures are open, whatever the species of the penalty; 'nos termos do artigo anterior e respectivos §§ 1º a 4º' brings in the regime of the measure (term, examinations, release, conversion), not the caput's species rule.

citations.cite: CP art. 98 — 'pela internação, ou tratamento ambulatorial', unconditioned

readings.description: 'nos termos do artigo anterior' carries the caput too: outpatient treatment only where the act is punishable with detenção.
readings.foreclosure: Art. 98 names both measures itself and then refers to 'o artigo anterior e respectivos §§ 1º a 4º' — the paragraphs that regulate a measure already chosen. A court reading the reference to include the caput would take this reading.

taken.rationale: Art. 98 names both measures without condition, and the reference that follows lists the paragraphs that regulate a measure's duration and end.

witnesses: cp-g1c-medidas-de-seguranca-testes.l4: art. 98 returns both measures

site.anchor: o tempo máximo da medida de segurança (art. 97, § 1º; Súmula 527 STJ)

source.quote: § 1º - A internação, ou tratamento ambulatorial, será por tempo indeterminado, perdurando enquanto não for averiguada, mediante perícia médica, a cessação de periculosidade. O prazo mínimo deverá ser de 1 (um) a 3 (três) anos. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: As printed: no maximum; the measure lasts until a medical examination finds the dangerousness has ceased.
readings.foreclosure: Foreclosed in STJ practice by Súmula 527; no court has struck it in abstract review as far as this sweep reached.

readings.description: Bounded by the maximum penalty abstractly cominated for the act committed.
Bounded by art. 75's general ceiling on time served (the line associated with the STF, not retrieved in this sweep; stated here without an authority quote).
readings.foreclosure: Not retrieved: portal.stf.jus.br was unreachable. Recorded so the encoder knows the STF line may differ from the STJ's.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 527 STJ, taken as the sweep proposes. The maximum is read with the case's causes at their outer limits, as for art. 109 (F-g1c-15); a fine-only preceito has no custodial maximum, and the encoding refuses there.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 527 STJ: 'O tempo de duração da medida de segurança não deve ultrapassar o limite máximo da pena abstratamente cominada ao delito praticado.' (julgado em 13/05/2015, DJe 18/05/2015)

witnesses: cp-g1c-medidas-de-seguranca-testes.l4: `homicídio, reclusão até 20` (twenty years) and `só multa` (REFUSED)

site.anchor: pode oferecer queixa ou prosseguir na ação em lugar do ofendido (art. 100, § 4º)

source.quote: § 4º - No caso de morte do ofendido ou de ter sido declarado ausente por decisão judicial, o direito de oferecer queixa ou de prosseguir na ação passa ao cônjuge, ascendente, descendente ou irmão.

readings.description: The right passes to the spouse, ascendant, descendant or sibling, as printed; a companheiro in a stable union is not listed.
The companheiro in a stable union takes the spouse's place, the Constitution recognising the stable union as a family entity.
readings.foreclosure: The Code lists 'cônjuge'. The constitutional argument (CF art. 226, § 3º) and any case law extending the list are outside this encoding's sources, and a list of who may prosecute is not widened by analogy without authority. A court may well take this reading.

taken.rationale: The encoding carries the list as printed; the extension to the companheiro needs an authority this encoding's sources do not include, and it is flagged in notes/g1c.md for a Brazilian lawyer.

witnesses: cp-g1c-acao-penal-testes.l4: `companheiro` — FALSE

site.anchor: a ação penal do crime complexo (art. 101)

source.quote: Art. 101 - Quando a lei considera como elemento ou circunstâncias do tipo legal fatos que, por si mesmos, constituem crimes, cabe ação pública em relação àquele, desde que, em relação a qualquer destes, se deva proceder por iniciativa do Ministério Público.

readings.description: Where any component crime is prosecuted on the Ministério Público's initiative, the complex crime's action is public, even over its own article's declaration of a private action; among the public actions in play, the least conditioned.

citations.cite: STF, Súmula 608 (cited by number only: its text could not be retrieved from an official source, see notes)

readings.description: Art. 101 applies only where the complex crime's own article states no action; where it declares a private action, that declaration governs as the more specific law.

citations.cite: CP art. 100, caput — 'salvo quando a lei expressamente a declara privativa do ofendido'

readings.rejection_rationale: Where the complex crime's article is silent, art. 100 already makes its action public, so on this reading art. 101 would have nothing to do.

taken.rationale: Only this reading gives art. 101 work to do. Which public action applies when the components' differ is the encoder's: the least conditioned, since art. 101 speaks of the Ministério Público proceeding on its own initiative.

witnesses: cp-g1c-acao-penal-testes.l4: a private-action complex crime with a public component — public
notes: Súmula 608 STF is cited by number only, on the conductor's ruling of 2026-09-30. An earlier version of this entry quoted its text from memory; that quotation was removed. Its text could not be retrieved from an official or LexML source on 2026-09-30: portal.stf.jus.br/jurisprudencia/sumariosumulas.asp?base=30&sumula=2694 and the STF's PDF of súmulas 1–736 returned HTTP 403 to this machine, and a fetch through another route failed STF's certificate check; LexML's URN resolver had no document for urn:lex:br:supremo.tribunal.federal;plenario:sumula:1984-10-17;608, and its search is behind a JavaScript check. sweep-a's S-sweep-a-08 also lists it as not retrieved.

That the súmula applies this reading of art. 101 is the encoder's recollection, not a checked fact. A Brazilian criminal lawyer should confirm its text, whether it rests on art. 101, and what it still reaches after art. 225's rewrite (sweep-c's range).

site.anchor: a representação ainda era retratável (art. 102)

source.quote: Art. 102 - A representação será irretratável depois de oferecida a denúncia.

citations.cite: CP art. 106, § 2º — 'Não é admissível o perdão depois que passa em julgado a sentença condenatória'

readings.description: Where the two acts fall on the same day, the dates do not say which came first; the encoding refuses by name rather than guess.

citations.cite: CP arts. 102 e 106, § 2º — 'depois de', an order the dates cannot show within a day

readings.description: An act on the same day as the barring event is in time, the bar running from the day after.
readings.foreclosure: 'depois de oferecida a denúncia' orders two acts, and a denúncia offered in the morning makes an afternoon retraction too late; the date alone cannot tell. The record of the hour would settle it.

readings.description: An act on the same day as the barring event is too late.
readings.foreclosure: The same objection the other way.

taken.rationale: Both provisions turn on the order of two acts, which a date does not carry within a day; the refusal names the missing fact.

witnesses: cp-g1c-acao-penal-testes.l4: retraction and denúncia on 10 March 2026 — REFUSED; pardon and trânsito on 10 March 2026 — REFUSED

site.anchor: os efeitos secundários da condenação subsistem (art. 107)

source.quote: II - pela anistia, graça ou indulto;

readings.description: Only the primary effect (the executória claim); secondary effects survive — the conviction still counts for reincidência, and the effects of arts. 91–92 stand.
Extinção da punibilidade by indulto extinguishes the conviction's effects generally, as anistia does.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 631 STJ. The encoding applies it to the indulto only, as the súmula is worded; for the graça, and for every cause the súmulas do not address, it refuses rather than extend them.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 631 STJ: 'O indulto extingue os efeitos primários da condenação (pretensão executória), mas não atinge os efeitos secundários, penais ou extrapenais.' (julgado em 24/04/2019, DJe 29/04/2019)

witnesses: cp-g1c-extincao-da-punibilidade-testes.l4: `indulto (art. 107, II)` — TRUE; `graça (art. 107, II)` — REFUSED

site.anchor: subsiste efeito condenatório da sentença (Súmula 18 STJ)

source.quote: Art. 120 - A sentença que conceder perdão judicial não será considerada para efeitos de reincidência. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: Declaratory of extinção da punibilidade; no condemnatory effect survives.
Condemnatory: art. 120 excludes only reincidência, so other effects (e.g. the duty to indemnify under art. 91, I) survive.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 18 STJ; art. 120's narrower words are the reincidência half of it.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 18 STJ: 'A sentença concessiva do perdão judicial é declaratória da extinção da punibilidade, não subsistindo qualquer efeito condenatório.' (julgado em 20/11/1990, DJ 28/11/1990)

witnesses: cp-g1c-extincao-da-punibilidade-testes.l4: `sentença que concede perdão judicial` — no condemnatory effect, not counted for reincidência

site.anchor: o prazo da multa antes do trânsito em julgado (art. 114)

source.quote: I - em 2 (dois) anos, quando a multa for a única cominada ou aplicada; (Incluído pela Lei nº 9.268, de 1º.4.1996)

readings.description: Before the conviction is final the fine is read as cominated; after, as applied. A fine cominated in the alternative ('ou multa') and applied alone therefore prescribes with the custodial penalty's period before the final judgment (II), and in two years after it (I).

citations.cite: CP art. 114 — 'cominada ou aplicada' against 'cominada ou cumulativamente aplicada'
CP arts. 109 e 110 — the same split between the penalty cominated and the penalty applied

readings.description: Once the fine alone has been applied, two years govern at every stage.
readings.foreclosure: Before the final judgment arts. 109–110 read the cominated penalty; applying inciso I's 'aplicada' there would measure the prosecution's prescription by a sentence that may still change. A court could still apply I as soon as a sentence imposes the fine alone.

taken.rationale: Read literally, a fine cominated in the alternative and applied alone falls under both incisos; the Code's own split between arts. 109 and 110 says which to read at which stage.

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `detenção de um a seis meses, ou multa` — three years before the final judgment; `o prazo da multa aplicada (art. 114)` NOTHING — two years after

site.anchor: os prazos de prescrição são reduzidos de metade (art. 115)

source.quote: Art. 115. São reduzidos de metade os prazos de prescrição quando o criminoso era, ao tempo do crime, menor de 21 (vinte e um) anos ou, na data da sentença, maior de 70 (setenta) anos, salvo se o crime envolver violência sexual contra a mulher. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 15.160, de 2025)

readings.description: 'na data da sentença' is the date of the first condemnatory decision: the sentence, or the acórdão where the conviction first comes on appeal; a later acórdão that confirms it does not move the date.
The date of the last condemnatory decision, a confirmatory acórdão included, so a convict who turns seventy while an appeal is pending gains the halving.
readings.foreclosure: The article says 'sentença', the decision that convicts; a confirming acórdão replaces it but does not convict anew. Case law on the point was not retrieved for this encoding.

taken.rationale: The input is named `data da sentença condenatória` and documented as the first conviction; which decision that is, where a court convicts on appeal, is for whoever supplies it.

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `Vicente, nascido em 10.6.1956`, crime of 1.8.2025 — sentence on 10.6.2026 (halved) and on 9.6.2026 (not)
notes: The rule refuses by name for every crime before 4.7.2025, the vigência of Lei nº 15.160/2025, whether or not the age engages the halving (the conductor's rulings of 2026-09-30; fork F-g1c-19). Measured: strict gate: 36 of 119 prescription assertions refuse; no prescription is computable for a crime before 4.7.2025 until the vintage pass brings the pre-2025 art. 115 into the bundle.
Sweep-a's copy of the 1984 wording (notes/g1c.md § 8) has the same age rule without the exception; a vintage pass that brings it into the bundle would restore every earlier crime's prescription.

site.anchor: o termo inicial da prescrição (art. 111)

source.quote: V - nos crimes contra a dignidade sexual ou que envolvam violência contra a criança e o adolescente, previstos neste Código ou em legislação especial, da data em que a vítima completar 18 (dezoito) anos, salvo se a esse tempo já houver sido proposta a ação penal.

citations.cite: CP art. 111, V (redação da Lei nº 14.344/2022)

readings.description: 'contra a criança e o adolescente' qualifies both kinds of crime: V reaches a crime against sexual dignity, or involving violence, whose victim was under eighteen at the time of the act.

citations.cite: CP art. 111, V — the period runs from the victim's eighteenth birthday, which only means something for a victim who was younger

readings.description: Every crime against sexual dignity, whatever the victim's age, runs from the victim's eighteenth birthday.
readings.rejection_rationale: For an adult victim the eighteenth birthday falls before the crime, so the period would run from before the act it prescribes; the inciso would then do nothing for adults and make no sense in its own terms.

taken.rationale: The inciso's term — the victim's eighteenth birthday — presupposes a victim under eighteen. The wording before 2022 (Lei nº 12.650/2012, as sweep-a reports it) said 'crimes contra a dignidade sexual de crianças e adolescentes', which points the same way; that text is outside the bundle and is noted, not relied on. 'a esse tempo já houver sido proposta' is read to include an action brought on the eighteenth birthday itself.

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `Ana, nascida em 1.1.1990` as victim — the general rule; Bia — from 1.3.2030; the action brought on 1.3.2030 — the general rule

site.anchor: a prescrição da pretensão punitiva (arts. 109 a 117)

source.quote: § 1o A prescrição, depois da sentença condenatória com trânsito em julgado para a acusação ou depois de improvido seu recurso, regula-se pela pena aplicada, não podendo, em nenhuma hipótese, ter por termo inicial data anterior à da denúncia ou queixa. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 12.234, de 2010).

citations.cite: CP art. 117, I — 'pelo recebimento da denúncia ou da queixa'

readings.description: 'data anterior à da denúncia ou queixa' is the date the denúncia or queixa was offered: the count by the penalty applied starts no earlier than that day.

citations.cite: CP art. 110, § 1º — 'a da denúncia ou queixa', the act itself

readings.description: It is the date the court received the denúncia or queixa, the act that interrupts prescription (art. 117, I).
readings.foreclosure: The paragraph names the denúncia, not its receipt, where art. 117, I names the receipt. The difference is the days between offering and receipt, which the interruption at receipt makes small; a court reading 'denúncia' as its receipt would take this reading.

taken.rationale: The paragraph speaks of the denúncia or queixa itself; art. 117 shows the Code naming the receipt when it means the receipt.

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `P5` — a crime of 2015 charged in 2019 is not prescribed by the penalty applied
notes: The 1984 § 2º, revoked by Lei nº 12.234/2010, spoke of 'data anterior à do recebimento da denúncia ou da queixa' (sweep-a's copy of Lei nº 7.209/1984, outside the bundle). The 2010 text drops 'recebimento'.

site.anchor: o último dia do prazo, descontadas as suspensões

source.quote: Art. 116 - Antes de passar em julgado a sentença final, a prescrição não corre: (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: The days on which prescription did not run are added, as days, to the last day of the period counted by the calendar.

citations.cite: CP art. 116 — 'a prescrição não corre' on those days

readings.description: The period still to run when the suspension began is counted again, by the calendar, from the day after it ends.

citations.cite: CP art. 10 — 'Contam-se os dias, os meses e os anos pelo calendário comum'

readings.foreclosure: The two differ by a day or two across month ends and leap years. The Code says only that prescription 'não corre'; adding the days that did not run is the smallest reading of that.

taken.rationale: What art. 116 takes out is days; putting the same number of days back keeps the count exact whatever months the suspension spans.

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: ten days in January 2022 push 31.12.2028 to 10.1.2029

site.anchor: a prescrição da pretensão executória

source.quote: VI - pela reincidência. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 9.268, de 1º.4.1996)

readings.description: The encoding takes the day of the interruption as supplied with the `reincidência (art. 117, VI)` event; which day that is, is decided by whoever supplies it, on one of the readings below.
The reincidência interrupts on the day the new crime is committed.
It interrupts on the day the conviction for the new crime becomes final, since only then is the convict a repeat offender (art. 63).

taken.rationale: 'pela reincidência' names no act and no day. The Code's definition of reincidência (art. 63) is g1b's, and case law on the day was not retrieved; the encoding records the question and takes the day as a fact.

site.anchor: as datas de interrupção da pretensão punitiva (art. 117, I a IV)

source.quote: II - pela pronúncia;

readings.description: Yes: the pronúncia interrupts regardless of the later reclassification.
No: once the jury reclassifies, the pronúncia is treated as never having interrupted prescription.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 191 STJ. The encoding has no field for a later reclassification: a pronúncia event interrupts on its day.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 191 STJ: 'A pronúncia é causa interruptiva da prescrição, ainda que o Tribunal do Júri venha a desclassificar o crime.' (julgado em 25/06/1997, DJ 01/08/1997)

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `P2b` — the pronúncia of 10.3.2020 restarts the count

site.anchor: aumento do art. 110, caput

source.quote: Art. 110 - A prescrição depois de transitar em julgado a sentença condenatória regula-se pela pena aplicada e verifica-se nos prazos fixados no artigo anterior, os quais se aumentam de um terço, se o condenado é reincidente. (Redação dada pela Lei nº 7.209, de 11.7.1984)

readings.description: No: the increase applies only to the executória prescription after final conviction; reincidência does not affect the punitive claim.
Yes, at least for § 1º, which also measures by the penalty applied and sits in the same article.

taken.rationale: Settled by Súmula 220 STJ. The increase is applied in `o prazo da prescrição da pretensão executória (arts. 110 e 115)` only; the punitive-claim periods have no field for reincidência.

settled_by.citation: Súmula 220 STJ: 'A reincidência não influi no prazo da prescrição da pretensão punitiva.' (julgado em 12/05/1999, DJ 19/05/1999)

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `E6` — five years and four months for the repeat offender's execution

site.anchor: as datas de interrupção da pretensão punitiva (art. 117, I a IV)

source.quote: IV - pela publicação da sentença ou acórdão condenatórios recorríveis;

citations.cite: CP art. 117, IV (redação da Lei nº 11.596/2007)

readings.description: Yes: a condemnatory acórdão always interrupts, including a confirmatory one, whatever it does to the penalty.
Only an acórdão that convicts for the first time (reversing an acquittal) or materially changes the penalty interrupts; a mere confirmation does not.

taken.rationale: Settled by the STF's Plenary thesis. Any `publicação do acórdão condenatório recorrível` event interrupts, with no field for whether it confirmed.

settled_by.citation: HC 176.473/RR (27/04/2020): 'Nos termos do inciso IV do artigo 117 do Código Penal, o Acórdão condenatório sempre interrompe a prescrição, inclusive quando confirmatório da sentença de 1º grau, seja mantendo, reduzindo ou aumentando a pena anteriormente imposta.'

witnesses: cp-g1c-prescricao-testes.l4: `P8` — an acórdão of 1.1.2024 restarts the count
